doc: What bounds a dispatching run. These numbers live here rather than in code for the same reason the model policy does: they are inside the evaluator fence, so a dispatched run cannot raise its own ceiling. They are checked against what the RUN LEDGER records, not against what a caller passes — `Dispatcher.prepare/2` used to read depth and remaining wall-clock out of its `parent` argument, which meant a caller that understated its depth was simply believed. A ceiling checked against a number the bounded thing supplies is not a ceiling.

depth.why: Depth is the axis on which a bounded thing becomes unbounded, and no per-step attempt count can see it: a run that spawns one run that spawns one run is three runs' worth of spend wearing one run's label. Derived by walking `parent_run` from the run's own file, so it is a fact about what happened rather than a claim about it.

wall_clock.why: Thirty minutes for a whole dispatch tree, not per run. A child inherits what is left of its parent's allowance and never a fresh one; the ledger's recorded spend is what 'left' means.

cost.why: A tree of dispatches spends real money and the first one that ran cost $0.17, so this is roughly thirty steps. It binds only on what an adapter actually reported: `claude -p` returns `total_cost_usd`, the API adapters return token counts and no price at all, and an unknown cost is recorded as unknown. It is NOT treated as zero — a zero would make this ceiling unreachable by exactly the adapters whose spend is hardest to see — and it is not treated as infinite either, because that would refuse every API dispatch. The honest consequence is stated rather than hidden: a run whose cost is unknown is bounded by depth and wall-clock alone, and says so.
